reason: The cited evidence confirms that HfMoTaTiZr has high strength (E2) and that Nb-containing alloys like HfMoNbTaTi show good ductility and elevated-temperature strength (E3), but it does not provide density data or direct comparisons of density and strength for Hf-replaced compositions, leaving the core premise of density reduction without sacrificing properties unsupported.
premises: Nb is significantly lighter than Hf, so replacing Hf with Nb reduces density.
Nb imparts effective solid-solution strengthening and ductility in RHEAs.
Substituting Hf with Nb preserves high-temperature strength up to ~1000 °C.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr has high RT strength (1600 MPa) and 800 °C strength (1045 MPa).
HfMoNbTaTi (Hf-free, Nb-containing) shows good RT ductility and high-temperature strength.
